title: Mind Stone Sequence
premise: A futuristic memory challenge where the player scans a short sequence of numbered tiles, then reconstructs the exact order after the tiles are shuffled into a lower pool.
interaction_model: Single-screen tap input on mobile or pointer devices; tap tiles to place them into the next open slot, tap placed tiles to send them back to the pool, and automatic validation occurs when all slots are filled.
objective: Memorize each displayed number pattern and rebuild it correctly to clear waves, earn score, and survive as long as possible.
progression: The run advances wave by wave, awarding more points per clear and gradually increasing sequence length from a small set toward a cap of six tiles, with one failed reconstruction ending the run.
theme: Sci-fi signal decoding and holographic terminal memory training.
mood: Focused, sleek, futuristic, lightly tense, and arcade-like.
likely_audience: players who enjoy memory games and minimalist sci-fi interfaces
confidence_notes: High confidence in the core loop because the full state machine, rendering flow, and input logic are visible in source.
Moderate confidence in the narrative framing because the fiction is mostly implied through UI language and visual styling rather than explicit story content.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first sci-fi memory puzzle game called "Mind Stone Sequence" presented as a holographic signal-decoding interface. Show a short sequence of unique numbered tiles across the upper portion of the screen and give the player a limited memorize phase with a visible timer bar. After the memorize time expires, shuffle those same numbered tiles into a lower pool and leave empty ghost slots above. The player should tap tiles from the pool to place them into the next open slot and tap placed tiles to return them to the pool if they want to correct the order. When all slots are filled, automatically verify the sequence against the original pattern. On success, award score, show satisfying positive feedback like particles, sound, and celebratory animated overlays, then advance to the next wave with a slightly harder sequence length progression capped around six tiles. On failure, trigger shake, failure audio, haptic-style feedback, and a game-over overlay with the final score and a reboot/restart button. Use a clean neon-blue and violet control-room aesthetic, a full-screen canvas presentation, futuristic HUD labels such as DATA and WAVE, responsive portrait-friendly layout, and a fast replayable arcade tone focused on short-term recall and order reconstruction.
